timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Edit
schema.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins

Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.content:
1	# Product
2	
3	## Register
4	
5	brand
6	
7	## Users
8	
9	Founders, developers and docs leads who have never heard of FirstRun. They land on the homepage cold, often from a link in a post. They read for about 10 seconds before they decide whether to stay. They are technical, but they are not here to read logs, traces or a financial model.
10	
11	## Product Purpose
12	
13	FirstRun checks documentation by running it. Two tools:
14	
15	- **Doc-test** runs a quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, fixes the docs and proves the fix in a second clean run. This is the main action. A visitor should paste a docs URL and run it.
16	- **Doc-audit** reads a repo's history and lists which docs pages went stale and which shipped features have no docs.
17	
18	Every run and every audit ends with a receipt: what it cost, which plan tier caps it, and the proof it passed. cfo.ai models the prices and caps. neatlogs traces every run. Entire records the build.
19	
20	Success: a new visitor can say in one sentence what Doc-test does, what Doc-audit does, and why the result can be trusted, then try Doc-test.
21	
22	## Brand Personality
23	
24	Calm, precise, confident. Apple-like: light mode, real logos, dead simple, big type, one idea per screen, the fewest steps.
25	
26	## Anti-References
27	
28	- A page that reads like a log, a dashboard or a report. If a section needs the reader to decode it, it fails.
29	- Walls of text, long subtitles under headings, three claims in one paragraph.
30	- Mixing Doc-test and Doc-audit in the same section. Each gets its own section, its own background color, and its own proof.
31	- Identical card grids, hero-metric templates, gradient text, glassmorphism.
32	- Internal build trivia (trace ids, hashes, hackathon plumbing) on the main path.
33	
34	## Design Principles
35	
36	1. One section, one idea, one sentence of explanation.
37	2. Doc-test, Doc-audit and the receipt story each have a different background so a new reader always knows which tool they are reading about.
38	3. Show the thing, not a description of it: a real broken step, a real fix, a real receipt.
39	4. H2s are centered and have no subtitle. Links are always underlined. Content is centered unless a layout needs otherwise.
40	5. Real PRs, real repos, real logos beat claims.
41	
42	## Accessibility & Inclusion
43	
44	WCAG AA contrast. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`. Never use color as the only signal. Underlined links. Works at 375 px wide with no sideways scroll.
45

1 """A receipt for one run: the work, its price, the tier caps, the proof it passed, and file hashes. 2 3 `firstrun receipt` reads runs//state.json and business/unit_economics.json, so the price and the 4 caps on a receipt are the same numbers cfo.ai models. The receipt hash and the evidence hashes let 5 `firstrun receipt --check` detect an edited receipt or an edited run folder. 6 """ 7 8 from __future__ import annotations 9 10 import hashlib 11 import html 12 import json 13 from datetime import datetime, timezone 14 from pathlib import Path 15 16 from firstrun import report 17 from firstrun.models import RunState, RunStatus, StepStatus 18 19 EVIDENCE = ("state.json", "runbook.json", "report.md") 20 UNHASHED = ("hash", "issued_at") 21 22 23 def _sha(data: bytes) -> str: 24 return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() 25 26 27 def body_hash(receipt: dict) -> str: 28 body = {k: v for k, v in receipt.items() if k not in UNHASHED} 29 return _sha(json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")) 30 31 32 def _caps(cost: float, tiers: dict, compute: float, bills: str | None) -> list[dict]: 33 rows = [] 34 for name, t in tiers.items(): 35 cap = float(t["cap_usd_per_run"]) 36 rev = t.get("revenue_per_run") 37 rows.append({ 38 "tier": name, 39 "bills_this_run": bool(bills) and name.lower() == bills.lower(), 40 "cap_usd": cap, 41 "used_pct": round(100 * cost / cap, 1) if cap > 0 else None, 42 "within_cap": cost <= cap, 43 "price_per_run_usd": rev, 44 "margin_pct": round(100 * (1 - (cost + compute) / rev), 1) if rev else None, 45 }) 46 return rows 47 48 49 def _proof(state: RunState, steps: int, passed: int) -> dict: 50 ok = state.status == RunStatus.VERIFIED 51 if ok: 52 claim = "A second clean container ran the patched steps with no model calls, and every step passed." 53 elif state.status == RunStatus.PASSED and not state.patches: 54 claim = "Every step passed on the first run. No fix was needed, so no second run was made." 55 else: 56 claim = f"The run ended {state.status.value}. Nothing here is verified." 57 return {"status": state.status.value, "verified": ok, "steps_passed": passed, "steps_total": steps, "claim": claim} 58 59 60 def build(state: RunState, run_dir: Path, econ: dict, bills: str | None = None, cfo_url: str = "", 61 steps_total: int | None = None) -> dict: 62 cost = round(state.usage.cost_usd, 4) 63 compute = float(econ["drivers"]["compute_per_run"]) 64 passed = sum(1 for s in state.step_status.values() if s == StepStatus.PASSED) 65 steps = steps_total if steps_total is not None else len(state.step_status) 66 first = state.first_failed_step 67 cls = state.classifications.get(first) if first is not None else None 68 evidence = {n: _sha((run_dir / n).read_bytes()) for n in EVIDENCE if (run_dir / n).exists()} 69 r = { 70 "receipt_id": f"FR-{state.run_id}", 71 "issued_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), 72 "work": { 73 "source_url": state.source_url, 74 "run_id": state.run_id, 75 "started_at": state.started_at, 76 "finished_at": state.finished_at, 77 "seconds": round(report._duration(state) or 0, 1), 78 "first_failed_step": first, 79 "failure_class": cls.top.value if cls else None, 80 "classified_by": cls.source if cls else None, 81 "patches": [{"step": p.step_id, "was": p.old_command, "now": p.new_command, "reason": p.reason} 82 for p in state.patches], 83 }, 84 "price": { 85 "model_cost_usd": cost, 86 "input_tokens": state.usage.input_tokens, 87 "output_tokens": state.usage.output_tokens, 88 "tool_calls": state.usage.tool_calls, 89 "compute_per_run_usd": compute, 90 "basis": "list price, not billed", 91 }, 92 "caps": _caps(cost, econ["tiers"], compute, bills), 93 "proof": _proof(state, steps, passed), 94 "audit": { 95 "run_id": state.run_id, 96 "tags": state.tags, 97 "evidence_sha256": evidence, 98 "caps_from": f"business/unit_economics.json, generated {econ.get('generated_at', 'unknown')}", 99 "margin_floor": econ.get("margin_floor"), 100 "cfo_model": cfo_url, 101 }, 102 } 103 r["hash"] = body_hash(r) 104 return r 105 106 107 def check(receipt_path: Path) -> list[str]: 108 """Problems found, empty when the receipt and the evidence files next to it are untouched.""" 109 r = json.loads(receipt_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) 110 problems = [] 111 if r.get("hash") != body_hash(r): 112 problems.append("the receipt was edited: its hash does not match its content") 113 for name, want in (r.get("audit", {}).get("evidence_sha256") or {}).items(): 114 f = receipt_path.parent / name 115 if not f.exists(): 116 problems.append(f"{name} is missing") 117 elif _sha(f.read_bytes()) != want: 118 problems.append(f"{name} changed after the receipt was issued") 119 return problems 120 121 122 def _flat(text: str, width: int) -> str: 123 """One line: backslash-newlines and newlines folded, long text cut.""" 124 flat = " ".join(text.replace("\\\n", " ").split()) 125 return flat if len(flat) <= width else flat[: width - 1].rstrip() + "..." 126 127 128 def _cell(text: str, width: int = 110) -> str: 129 """A Markdown table cell: one line, pipes escaped.""" 130 return _flat(text, width).replace("|", "\\|") 131 1	"""Publish a run to the public site log: docs/runs/<run id>.txt plus one row in docs/runs/index.json.
2	
3	The repo is public and Netlify serves docs/, so a committed row is a run anyone can replay.
4	"""
5	
6	from __future__ import annotations
7	
8	import json
9	import os
10	import re
11	from pathlib import Path
12	
13	from firstrun import share
14	
15	INDEX = "index.json"
16	
17	
18	def find_site_dir(start: Path | None = None) -> Path | None:
19	    """docs/runs of the firstrun checkout. FIRSTRUN_SITE_DIR wins, then the cwd and its parents."""
20	    env = os.environ.get("FIRSTRUN_SITE_DIR")
21	    if env:
22	        p = Path(env)
23	        return p if p.is_dir() else None
24	    here = (start or Path.cwd()).resolve()
25	    for base in [here, *here.parents]:
26	        cand = base / "docs" / "runs"
27	        if (cand / INDEX).exists():
28	            return cand
29	    return None
30	
31	
32	def _first_error(step: dict) -> str:
33	    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in (step.get("error_tail") or "").splitlines() if ln.strip()]
34	    if not lines:
35	        return ""
36	    bad = [ln for ln in lines if re.search(r"error|not found|no module|cannot|can't|failed|denied|timed out|exit", ln, re.I)]
37	    return bad[-1][:140] if bad else ""
38	
39	
40	def _summary(p: dict) -> str:
41	    steps = p["steps"]
42	    skipped = [s for s in steps if s["skipped"]]
43	    ran = [s for s in steps if not s["skipped"]]
44	    failed = [s for s in ran if s["status"] in ("failed", "gave_up", "needs_human")]
45	    if not steps:
46	        return "Stopped before any step ran."
47	    if failed:
48	        s = failed[0]
49	        err = _first_error(s)
50	        return f"Step {s['id']} broke: {s['intent']}." + (f" {err}" if err else "")
51	    bits = [f"{sum(1 for s in ran if s['status'] == 'passed')} of {len(ran)} runnable steps passed."]
52	    if p["patches"]:
53	        bits.append(f"{len(p['patches'])} fix{'es' if len(p['patches']) != 1 else ''} proven in a fresh container.")
54	    if skipped:
55	        bits.append(f"{len(skipped)} skipped: {skipped[0]['skip_reason'].rstrip('.')}.")
56	    return " ".join(bits)
57	
58	
59	def _cost(run_dir: Path) -> float:
60	    """List-price model cost in dollars, to 4 places. The share payload rounds to cents."""
61	    try:
62	        return round(float(json.loads((run_dir / "state.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["usage"]["cost_usd"]), 4)
63	    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
64	        return 0.0
65	
66	
67	def row_for(payload: dict, cost: float | None = None) -> dict:
68	    counted = [s for s in payload["steps"] if not s["skipped"]]
69	    ver = payload["verify"]
70	    return {
71	        "id": payload["run_id"],
72	        "ts": payload.get("started_at") or "",
73	        "target": payload["target"],
74	        "title": payload["title"] or payload["target"],
75	        "url": payload["source_url"],
76	        "status": payload["status"],
77	        "passed": ver["steps_passed"],
78	        "total": len(payload["steps"]),
79	        "runnable": len(counted),
80	        "skipped": len(payload["steps"]) - len(counted),
81	        "fixes": len(payload["patches"]),
82	        "seconds": round(payload.get("time_to_first_success_s") or 0),
83	        "cost": payload.get("cost_usd", 0) if cost is None else cost,
84	        "fixture": bool(payload.get("fixture")),
85	        "summary": _summary(payload),
86	    }
87	
88	
89	def publish_run(run_dir, site_dir: Path | None = None) -> Path | None:
90	    """Write the replay file and upsert the index row. Returns the replay file, or None off-site."""
91	    site = site_dir or find_site_dir()
92	    if site is None:
93	        return None
94	    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
95	    payload = share.build_payload(run_dir)
96	    run_id = payload["run_id"]
97	    site.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
98	    out = site / f"{run_id}.txt"
99	    out.write_text(share.encode(payload) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
100	    idx_path = site / INDEX
101	    try:
102	        doc = json.loads(idx_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
103	    except (OSError, ValueError):
104	        doc = {}
105	    rows = [r for r in doc.get("runs", []) if r.get("id") != run_id]
106	    rows.append(row_for(payload, _cost(run_dir)))
107	    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r.get("ts", ""), reverse=True)
108	    idx_path.write_text(json.dumps({"runs": rows}, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
109	    return out
110	
111	
112	def publish_all(runs_dir, site_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
113	    """Backfill every finished run folder. Returns how many were published."""
114	    n = 0
115	    for d in sorted(Path(runs_dir).glob("*")):
116	        if (d / "state.json").exists() and (d / "runbook.json").exists():
117	            try:
118	                if publish_run(d, site_dir):
119	                    n += 1
120	            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - one broken run folder never stops the backfill
121	                continue
122	    return n

1	"""Run by .github/workflows/audit-request.yml. Turns an audit-request issue into a board on the doc-audit log.
2	
3	Reads ISSUE_BODY, ISSUE_LABELS (comma separated) and EVENT_LABEL from the environment, never from argv,
4	so issue text never reaches a shell. Writes `id`, `repo`, `message` and `publish` to GITHUB_OUTPUT.
5	"""
6	
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import json
10	import os
11	import subprocess
12	import sys
13	import urllib.request
14	from pathlib import Path
15	
16	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src"))
17	
18	from firstrun import audit as audit_mod, intake  # noqa: E402
19	
20	SITE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "docs" / "audits"
21	
22	
23	def out(**kv: str) -> None:
24	    path = os.environ.get("GITHUB_OUTPUT")
25	    lines = []
26	    for k, v in kv.items():
27	        lines.append(f"{k}<<EOF_INTAKE\n{v}\nEOF_INTAKE")
28	    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
29	    if path:
30	        with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
31	            f.write(text)
32	    print(text)
33	
34	
35	def from_gist(gid: str) -> dict:
36	    p = subprocess.run(["gh", "api", f"gists/{gid}"], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
37	    if p.returncode != 0:
38	        raise ValueError("the gist could not be read")
39	    files = json.loads(p.stdout).get("files") or {}
40	    f = next((f for f in files.values() if str(f.get("filename", "")).endswith(".json")), None)
41	    if not f:
42	        raise ValueError("the gist has no .json file")
43	    if (f.get("size") or 0) > intake.MAX_BYTES:
44	        raise ValueError("the audit is larger than 3 MB")
45	    text = f.get("content") or ""
46	    raw = str(f.get("raw_url") or "")
47	    if f.get("truncated") and raw.startswith("https://gist.githubusercontent.com/"):
48	        with urllib.request.urlopen(raw, timeout=30) as r:  # noqa: S310 - fixed https host checked above
49	            text = r.read(intake.MAX_BYTES + 1).decode("utf-8")
50	    return intake.validate(json.loads(text))
51	
52	
53	def main() -> int:
54	    fields = intake.parse_issue(os.environ.get("ISSUE_BODY", ""))
55	    labels = {x.strip() for x in os.environ.get("ISSUE_LABELS", "").split(",") if x.strip()}
56	    event_label = os.environ.get("EVENT_LABEL", "")
57	    repo, gid = fields["repo"], fields["gist"]
58	
59	    if gid:
60	        if "publish" not in labels:
61	            out(publish="no", message=(
62	                f"Thanks. This offers a private audit of `{repo or 'your repo'}` for the public log. "
63	                "A maintainer reads the gist and adds the `publish` label to put it on the board."))
64	            return 0
65	        try:
66	            doc = from_gist(gid)
67	        except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
68	            out(publish="no", message=f"The submission could not be published: {e}.")
69	            return 0
70	        audit_mod.publish(doc, SITE_DIR)
71	        out(publish="yes", id=doc["id"], repo=doc["repo"],
72	            message=f"Published. The board for `{doc['repo']}` is at {intake.SITE}?id={doc['id']}")
73	        return 0
74	
75	    if event_label and event_label != "audit-request":
76	        out(publish="no", message="")
77	        return 0
78	    if not repo:
79	        out(publish="no", message="The issue names no repo. Write it as owner/repo, for example fastapi/typer.")
80	        return 0
81	    try:
82	        result = audit_mod.audit(repo, 180, use_jev=bool(os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY")))
83	    except (RuntimeError, ValueError) as e:
84	        msg = str(e)
85	        if "clone failed" in msg:
86	            msg = (f"FirstRun could not clone `{repo}`. If it is private, run "
87	                   f"`firstrun audit {repo}` on your machine, then `firstrun audit-submit` to offer it for the log.")
88	        out(publish="no", message=f"The audit did not finish: {msg}")
89	        return 0
90	    audit_mod.publish(result, SITE_DIR)
91	    s = result["summary"]
92	    out(publish="yes", id=result["id"], repo=result["repo"], message=(
93	        f"Done. `{result['repo']}`: {s['pages']} docs pages, {s['stale']} stale, "
94	        f"{s['uncovered']} recent features with no docs, {s['cards']} cards.\n\n"
95	        f"Board: {intake.SITE}?id={result['id']} (live about a minute after this comment)."))
96	    return 0
97	
98	
99	if __name__ == "__main__":
100	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	name: doc-audit intake
2	
3	# An audit-request issue becomes a board on the doc-audit log.
4	# Public repo: audited here on open. Private submission: published when a maintainer adds the publish label.
5	on:
6	  issues:
7	    types: [opened, labeled]
8	
9	permissions:
10	  contents: write
11	  issues: write
12	
13	concurrency:
14	  group: doc-audit-log
15	  cancel-in-progress: false
16	
17	jobs:
18	  audit:
19	    if: contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'audit-request') && (github.event.action == 'opened' || github.event.label.name == 'publish')
20	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
21	    timeout-minutes: 20
22	    steps:
23	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
24	        with:
25	          ref: main
26	      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
27	        with:
28	          python-version: "3.11"
29	      - run: pip install -e .
30	      - id: intake
31	        # Issue text reaches the script only through env vars, never through the shell.
32	        run: python scripts/audit_intake.py
33	        env:
34	          ISSUE_BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
35	          ISSUE_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ',') }}
36	          EVENT_LABEL: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
37	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
38	          TYPESAFE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }}
39	          NEATLOGS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NEATLOGS_API_KEY }}
40	          FIRSTRUN_ENV_FILE: /dev/null
41	      - if: steps.intake.outputs.publish == 'yes'
42	        env:
43	          REPO: ${{ steps.intake.outputs.repo }}
44	          NUM: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
45	        run: |
46	          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
47	          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
48	          git add docs/audits
49	          git commit -m "Doc-audit log: add $REPO (issue #$NUM)"
50	          git pull --rebase origin main
51	          git push origin HEAD:main
52	      - if: steps.intake.outputs.message != ''
53	        env:
54	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
55	          NUM: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
56	          MSG: ${{ steps.intake.outputs.message }}
57	        run: gh issue comment "$NUM" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --body "$MSG"
58	      - if: steps.intake.outputs.publish == 'yes'
59	        env:
60	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
61	          NUM: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
62	        run: gh issue close "$NUM" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --reason completed

    """Audit a repo's docs: stale pages, features with no docs, and proposal cards. TARGET is owner/repo, a GitHub URL, a git folder, or a docs site with a sitemap."""
    from firstrun import audit as audit_mod, tracing

    tracing.init_tracing(tags=["audit"])
    try:
        if re.match(r"^(https?://)?[\w.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}(/|$)", target) and "github.com" not in target:
            result = audit_mod.audit_sitemap(target, stale_days)
        else:
            click.echo(f"auditing {target}: cloning history, no checkout")
            result = audit_mod.audit(target, stale_days, use_jev=not no_jev, docs_repo=docs_repo)
    except (RuntimeError, ValueError) as e:
        tracing.close_tracing()
        raise click.ClickException(str(e)) from e
    out_dir = Path(config.RUNS_DIR) / result["id"]
    md = audit_mod.save(result, out_dir)
    s = result["summary"]
    click.echo(f"{s['pages']} pages: {s['stale']} stale, {s['quiet']} quiet, {s['aging']} aging, {s['fresh']} fresh"
               + (f", {s['unchecked']} unchecked" if s.get("unchecked") else "") + f". Oldest {s['oldest_days']} days.")
    click.echo(f"{s['features']} recent features, {s['uncovered']} with no docs. {s['cards']} proposal cards.")
    click.echo(f"report: {md}")
    click.echo(f"issue: firstrun audit-issue {result['id']}")
    if not no_publish:
        site = audit_mod.find_audit_site()
        if site:
            click.echo(f"site log: {audit_mod.publish(result, site)} (commit docs/audits to show it on the site)")
    tracing.close_tracing()

def test_features_coverage_momentum_and_cards(repo):
    a = audit.audit(str(repo), use_jev=False)
    feats = {f["term"]: f for f in a["features"]}
    assert feats["--format"]["covered"] is False
    kinds = {c["kind"] for c in a["cards"]}
    assert {"document", "refresh", "automate", "quickstart"} <= kinds
    assert any(c["kind"] == "content" for c in a["cards"])  # export has 3+ commits in the window
    assert a["release"]["name"] == "v1.1" and a["release"]["previous"] == "v1.0"
    notes = a["drafts"]["release_notes"]
    assert "## New" in notes and "--format" in notes and "bump deps" not in notes
    assert a["summary"]["pages"] == 4


def test_save_and_publish_upsert_one_row(repo, tmp_path):
    a = audit.audit(str(repo), use_jev=False)
    md = audit.save(a, tmp_path / "out")
    assert md.read_text(encoding="utf-8").startswith("# Docs audit")
    site = tmp_path / "audits"
    audit.publish(a, site)
    audit.publish(a, site)
    rows = json.loads((site / "index.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["audits"]
    assert len(rows) == 1 and rows[0]["stale"] == a["summary"]["stale"]
    assert json.loads((site / f"{a['id']}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["repo"] == a["repo"]


def test_jev_sort_without_key_is_empty(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("TYPESAFE_API_KEY", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(audit.config, "load_env", lambda *a, **k: None)
    assert audit.jev_sort(["something"]) == {}


def test_title_skips_html_and_falls_back_to_the_file_name():
    assert audit._title("# <style>\n", "docs/index.md") == "Index"
    assert audit._title("---\ntitle: Export data\n---\n", "docs/x.md") == "Export data"
    assert audit._title("# Use `--format`\n", "docs/x.md") == "Use --format"


def test_internal_docs_are_not_user_pages():
    assert not audit.is_doc_path("docs/internal/plan.md")
    assert not audit.is_doc_path("docs/2026-06-23-tui-adr.md")
    assert not audit.is_doc_path("docs/RELEASING.md")
    assert audit.is_doc_path("docs/configure/commands.md")


def test_repo_name_never_marks_a_topic(repo):
    commits = audit.read_history(repo)
    pages = {p["path"]: p for p in audit.analyze_pages(commits, ["docs/export.md"], {}, NOW, 180, repo_name="acme/export")}
    assert pages["docs/export.md"]["relevant_since"] == 0


def test_release_range_skips_nightly_tags():
    t = lambda n, d: {"name": n, "date": NOW - timedelta(days=d)}
    commits = [{"sha": "a", "date": NOW - timedelta(days=3), "subject": "feat: x", "files": [], "author": "a", "scope": ""}]
    rel = audit.release_range(commits, [t("v2.0-nightly.1", 1), t("v1.1", 2), t("v1.0", 10)], NOW)
    assert rel["name"] == "v1.1" and rel["previous"] == "v1.0"


def test_issue_lists_cards_and_never_opens_anything(repo):
    a = audit.audit(str(repo), use_jev=False)
    a["url"] = "https://github.com/acme/proj"
    a["repo"] = "acme/proj"
    data = audit.issue(a)
    assert data["title"].startswith("Docs audit:")
    assert "- [ ] **Refresh docs/export.md**" in data["body"]
    assert data["commands"] == [f'gh issue create --repo acme/proj --title "{data["title"]}" --body-file issue.md']


def test_publish_keeps_one_audit_per_repo(repo, tmp_path):
    site = tmp_path / "audits"
    a1 = audit.audit(str(repo), use_jev=False)
    audit.publish(a1, site)
    a2 = dict(a1, id=a1["id"] + "-b")
    audit.publish(a2, site)
    rows = json.loads((site / "index.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["audits"]

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

from firstrun import publish, share

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures_report"


def _run(tmp_path, name="run-verified") -> Path:
    dst = tmp_path / name
    shutil.copytree(FIXTURES / name, dst)
    return dst


def test_publish_writes_replay_and_row(tmp_path):
    site = tmp_path / "docs" / "runs"
    out = publish.publish_run(_run(tmp_path), site)
    doc = json.loads((site / "index.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert len(doc["runs"]) == 1
    row = doc["runs"][0]
    assert out == site / f"{row['id']}.txt"
    assert share.decode(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["run_id"] == row["id"]
    assert row["total"] >= row["passed"]


def test_publish_twice_keeps_one_row(tmp_path):
    site = tmp_path / "runs"
    run = _run(tmp_path)
    publish.publish_run(run, site)
    publish.publish_run(run, site)
    assert len(json.loads((site / "index.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["runs"]) == 1


def test_publish_off_site_is_a_no_op(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("FIRSTRUN_SITE_DIR", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    assert publish.publish_run(_run(tmp_path)) is None

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- the bill and the site copy

def _receipt(tmp_path, **kw):
    s = _state(**kw)
    return receipt.build(s, _run_dir(tmp_path, s), ECON, bills="team")

    page = receipt.render_html(r)
    assert "$0.0453" in page and "$0.0020" in page and "$0.0473" in page

    assert "firstrun receipt --check docs/receipts/FR-20261011-000000-example.json" in page
    assert "—" not in page and "–" not in page


def test_money_keeps_tiny_amounts_readable():
    assert receipt.money(0.0) == "$0.0000"
    assert receipt.money(0.000557) == "$0.000557"
    assert receipt.money(0.0453) == "$0.0453"
    assert receipt.money(None) == "Not recorded"

    assert "Not recorded" in audit_page

    assert receipt.index_fields(old) == {"receipt": "FR-audit-20261011-000000-acme-widgets", "receipt_usd": None}


def test_publish_site_keeps_the_first_issue_time(tmp_path):
    r = _receipt(tmp_path)
    out = tmp_path / "receipts"
    receipt.publish_site({**r, "issued_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}, out)
    receipt.publish_site(r, out)
    saved = json.loads((out / f"{r['receipt_id']}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert saved["issued_at"] == "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" and saved["hash"] == receipt.body_hash(saved)
    assert (out / f"{r['receipt_id']}.html").exists()
    assert receipt.billed_tier(out, r["receipt_id"]) == "Team"

    (d / "runbook.json").write_text("{", encoding="utf-8")  # unreadable runbook: steps fall back to the state
    docs = tmp_path / "docs"
    (docs / "runs").mkdir(parents=True)
    (docs / "audits").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "business").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "business" / "unit_economics.json").write_text(json.dumps(ECON), encoding="utf-8")

input.content:
Receipts look like a bill, and every run and audit links to one

- receipt.py: a new bill layout for runs and audits. Torn top and bottom
  edges, itemized lines with a total, a bar per tier cap (over cap is
  hatched and labeled), a proof stamp, a hash stub with a barcode, and a
  two-column print layout that fits one page. Self-contained, 375 px safe.
- firstrun receipt --all-published writes a receipt into docs/receipts for
  every run and audit the site lists, and adds receipt and receipt_usd to
  each index row. Old audits say "Not recorded". Rows with a redacted id
  map to their run folder by prefix and URL.
- publish_run and audit.publish now write the item's receipt too. The
  audit workflow commits docs/receipts.
- receipt --check finds the evidence in runs/<id>/ for a docs/receipts copy.
- doc-test and doc-audit: a View receipt pill with the total on every list

All five tasks are done and committed on branch `worktree-agent-a898be48d0f6e119d` as **ff46d01**; the full suite gives **314 passed, 64 skipped, 1 xfailed**. One choice differs from your spec: the "View receipt" button shows the bill's total (model usage plus compute), not model cost alone. The bill adds both lines, so a button showing model cost would never match the bill's total. For the accuknox run the button reads `View receipt · $0.0473` and the bill lists model usage $0.0453 plus compute $0.0020. If you want model cost on the button instead, it is a one-line change to `total_usd()` in `receipt.py`.

**Branch base.** The worktree did not contain `render_audit_html` or `PRODUCT.md`. Both are in commit 2f5ee0d on `feat/audit-receipt`, the main checkout's HEAD and a direct child of my start point. I fast-forwarded onto it, so my branch contains 2f5ee0d followed by ff46d01.

**Receipt design** (`src/firstrun/receipt.py`; `render_md` and `body_hash` inputs unchanged):
- **Paper:** a warm off-white sheet, 600 px wide, on a grey desk. Top and bottom edges are torn with a CSS conic-gradient mask. A dashed perforation with half-circle notches separates the stub.
- **Header:** the real FirstRun logo, "Receipt" with "Doc-test run" or "Doc-audit" under it, receipt number, date and issue date. A "For" box links the docs page or the repo.
- **Items:** right-aligned monospaced amounts and a heavy rule above TOTAL.
  - Run: Model usage with token counts, then Compute.
  - Audit: Clone and history scan ($0.0000), then Jev reads with calls and tokens, or "Not recorded".
  - Amounts show 4 decimals, or 6 when a nonzero amount is under $0.001.
- **Tier caps:** one bar per tier. Within cap is a solid blue fill. Over cap is an amber hatched fill, a ▲ marker and the words "over cap", so red is never the only signal. Billed tier, price and margin show beside each bar. Audits show a commits-read bar against the 20,000 limit instead.
- **Proof stamp:** a rotated double-border stamp. Green "Verified" or "Passed as written", a dashed grey "Not verified", or an amber "n of m cards cited".
- **Stub:** receipt hash, evidence hashes, a `firstrun receipt --check docs/receipts/<id>.json` line, a decorative barcode drawn from the hash, and "List prices, not billed."
- **Behaviour:** no external requests (the page loads only itself). It renders with optional fields missing, and its two animations are switched off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Print:** two columns with a dashed column rule. Headless Edge prints the largest receipt (8 fixes), the accuknox run and an audit each on one page.

**Receipts generated:** 76 receipts (152 files) in `docs/receipts/`.
- All 68 runs in `docs/runs/index.json`.
- All 7 audits in `docs/audits/index.json`. All 7 have no recorded cost and say "Not recorded".
- The existing `FR-audit-20261011-091731` HTML, redrawn in the new design.

New command: `firstrun receipt --all-published`. It also adds `receipt` and `receipt_usd` fields to each index row.

**Buttons:**
- **Doc-test:** a "View receipt · $X" pill under every list row, kept outside the row link so it is valid HTML, and a button in the run header. I removed the now-duplicate "$x model cost" text from list rows. I renamed the header's "Cost" fact to "Model cost" so it does not look like a second total.
- **Doc-audit:** the same pill on every list row, plus a header button on each board. The board version fetches the receipt JSON. Old audits show a muted "no cost recorded".
- All pills are focusable with the keyboard (checked with Tab).

**Keeping receipts current:**
- `publish_run` and `audit.publish` now write the item's receipt too. Neither step ever blocks publishing.
- `firstrun audit` passes its run folder so evidence files get hashed.
- The workflow now runs `git add docs/audits docs/receipts`. `scripts/audit_intake.py` needed no change because it calls `audit.publish`.
- `receipt --check` on a copy in `docs/receipts` now finds the evidence in `runs/<id>/`. I confirmed it reports "ok" on 4 real receipts.

**Browser checks** (my own tab, port 8761, no console errors anywhere):
- A run receipt and an audit receipt at 1280 px and 375 px. At 375 px the page is exactly as wide as the screen, so there is no sideways scroll.
- Both tool-page lists at desktop and 375 px.
- The run-view button and the board button.
- Screenshots are in the session's `tool-results` folder. The single-page print PDFs are in the scratchpad.

**Found in passing, worth a separate fix:** 4 rows in `docs/runs/index.json`, and their `docs/runs/*.txt` files, have the literal id `...-fla[REDACTED]`. The redactor read `flask-palletsprojects-com` as a secret key and mangled the run id when the runs were published. I mapped those rows to their real folders by timestamp prefix plus matching URL, so their receipts are correct, but the redactor still needs a fix.
